demonstration.narration: Traffic is steady, but this dashboard only counts requests with http.route. I'll search schema.route_present: false for the requests without a route, then compare what they have in common.
demonstration.evidence: The hit count now shows how many requests were recorded without http.route. These requests still happened, but a dashboard counting only requests with that field leaves them out. Next, we compare what they have in common.

isolate.concept: Requests without a route still happened, but their http.route field is missing. A dashboard that counts only requests with that field leaves them out.
isolate.evidence: The hit count shows requests with no http.route. These requests still happened, but the route-based dashboard count leaves them out.

inspect.title: Look for what these requests share
inspect.concept: Field statistics counts the distinct values of every field at once. A field with one value across all these requests is something they share.
inspect.narration: Switch from Documents to Field statistics. It counts the distinct values of each column for the requests in view. Look for a column about where a request came from (producer, version or host) with one value across all of them.
inspect.reasoning: The route could have gone missing in the telemetry SDK, in one service's release or on one server. Field statistics shows every field's distinct values at once, so you don't have to guess.
inspect.evidence: One field has a single value across every request without a route.

demonstration.narration: I'll switch to Field statistics, which counts the distinct values of every field for the requests without a route.
demonstration.reasoning: Any field could set these requests apart, so we scan them all instead of guessing one. A field with one value across every request is something they share, unless our own query put that one value there.
demonstration.evidence: Every request without a route has the same ${param.facet.field}, while ${param.facet.others} each have several values. schema.route_present shows one value only because our query asked for it. Each .keyword row repeats the field above it. So the ${param.facet.noun} is what these requests share. The ${param.facet.field} column shows which ${param.facet.noun} it is.

checks.title: Time window
checks.detail: We set the time window to cover the drop in the dashboard's count.

checks.title: Missing routes
checks.detail: We searched for requests that arrived without a route, the ones the dashboard leaves out.

checks.title: What they share
checks.detail: We compared every field of those requests at once and found the ${param.facet.noun} they all share.

checks.title: The other side
checks.detail: We searched the requests that kept their route for that ${param.facet.noun}, and found none.

answer.evidence: The query for missing routes found ${truth.scope} requests the dashboard leaves out. Field statistics and an empty boolean query tie them to ${truth.finding}.

goal.title: Check the requests that kept their route
goal.concept: A boolean query joins conditions with and, or and not. Asking for what shouldn't exist turns an empty result into evidence.
goal.narration: Now check the other side. Search for requests that have a route and also the value the requests without one share. If nothing matches, that value goes only with the missing route.
goal.reasoning: Every request without a route shares one value. That explains the missing routes only if no request with a route has it too.
goal.evidence: The query finds nothing, so only requests without a route have that value.

demonstration.narration: I'll search for requests that have a route and the shared value too. I expect no results, which would show that value goes only with the missing route.
demonstration.reasoning: Every request without a route shares one value. That explains the missing routes only if no request with a route has it, and a boolean query asks exactly that.
demonstration.evidence: No results: no request with a route has ${param.facet.field} ${param.facet.value}. So the route goes missing only there. ${truth.conclusion}

hints: Check whether any request that kept its route shares the value you found.
In the query bar, join two conditions with and. The first keeps requests that have a route. The second is the value the others share, in quotes. Here, no results is the answer you want.
Type schema.route_present: true and ${param.facet.field}: "${param.facet.value}"; Show me can do it for you.
